title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
input_format: First line contains integer `n`, followed by `n` non-negative bar heights.

sample_tests.explanation: Elevation map traps 6 units of water.

hints: The water trapped above bar i is min(max_left, max_right) - height[i].
Use two pointers from left and right inward.
Advance whichever side has the smaller maximum height.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    h = [int(x) for x in data[1:1+n]]
    l, r = 0, n - 1
    l_max = r_max = ans = 0
    while l < r:
        if h[l] < h[r]:
            if h[l] >= l_max: l_max = h[l]
            else: ans += l_max - h[l]
            l += 1
        else:
            if h[r] >= r_max: r_max = h[r]
            else: ans += r_max - h[r]
            r -= 1
    print(ans)
